name: CHAdeMO
description: DC-only charging interface defined by the CHAdeMO Association and standardised as configuration AA of IEC 62196-3, used with DC EV supply equipment of System A (IEC 61851-23 Annex AA). The circular face has two large DC contacts side by side between two groups of signal contacts. The CHAdeMO protocol versions 0.9 to 2.x share this connector; CHAdeMO 3.0 uses the different ChaoJi connector.

mechanicalNotes: Ten contact positions: two large DC contacts side by side, a group of four signal positions above and a group of four below; one manufacturer specification marks one upper position as an empty circuit.
Electrically latched to the inlet during charging.

electricalProfiles.name: DC (IEC 62196-3 configuration AA)
conditions: Maximum rating of configuration AA in IEC 62196-3:2022 (edition 2.0), tables 301 and 303.
IEC 62196-3:2026 (edition 3.0) announces increased ratings for all configurations; they are not recorded here yet.

Contact functions of configuration AA (table 301; position numbers do not give the location): DC+ and DC− 1000 V, 400 A; control pilots CP, CP2 and CP3 30 V, 10 A; communication COM1 (+) and COM2 (−) 30 V, 2 A; isolation monitor IM 30 V, 2 A; proximity detection or connection switch (PP or CS) 30 V, 2 A; optional auxiliary power supply AUX1 30 V, 10 A.
Table 301 lists no protective earth position for configuration AA; a PE contact is required only for use with non-isolated DC EV supply equipment.
Used only with DC EV supply equipment of System A (IEC 61851-23 Annex AA).
Products are rated individually; for example one vehicle connector specification gives 125 A, 100 A or 60 A at 500 V DC depending on the cable.

The values come from IEC 62196-3, whose sample does not name CHAdeMO; the identification of CHAdeMO with configuration AA comes from a secondary source, consistent with a CHAdeMO connector specification referring to IEC 62196-3.

electricalProfiles.name: DC, CHAdeMO protocol 0.9
conditions: Figures from a secondary source (125 A × 500 V DC, 62.5 kW); the CHAdeMO Association pages reviewed give no figures for versions 0.9, 1.0 and 1.1.
The CHAdeMO Association states that most CHAdeMO chargers deployed worldwide follow protocol 0.9.

electricalProfiles.name: DC, CHAdeMO protocol 1.2
conditions: CHAdeMO 1.2 (March 2017): 400 A × 500 V, up to 200 kW.

electricalProfiles.name: DC, CHAdeMO protocol 2.0
conditions: CHAdeMO 2.0 (released to Regular members on 29 May 2018): 400 A × 1 kV, up to 400 kW, with the exact same plug shape.
The Association describes high-power charging at this level with liquid-cooled cable assemblies (or pantographs).

sources.title: CHAdeMO
sources.note: Secondary source for the protocol 0.9 rating only.

notes: Contacts and genders are not recorded: IEC 62196-3:2022 table 301 lists the configuration AA contact functions without positions, and the manufacturer specification shows the connector positions 1 to 10 without functions or genders. Mapping functions to positions would rely on secondary sources only.
Protective earth conflict: table 301 gives no PE position for configuration AA, while secondary pinouts describe a frame-ground contact; protectiveEarth is left null.
No face is drawn: the only reviewed face (JAE FF-00368H, vehicle connector) gives neither contact functions nor genders, and no vehicle inlet face was reviewed.
Protocol versions 1.0 (2012) and 1.1 have no ratings in the reviewed Association pages and are not modelled; 0.9 relies on Wikipedia (confidence medium).

CHAdeMO 3.0 (ChaoJi connector) is out of this family. Association pages give two dates: released to Regular members on 24 April 2020 (CHAdeMO 3.0 page), "published in April 2021" (protocol development page).
DC ratings of configuration AA come from the 2022 edition; the increased ratings of IEC 62196-3:2026 are not reviewed yet.
Other standards carrying CHAdeMO (IEC 61851-24 communication, IEEE adoption, Japanese JEVS documents) were not reviewed.
The EVicons plug-chademo icon (0.8.0) is not attached: no vehicle inlet face was reviewed, and the icon draws 6 of the 10 contact positions recorded for the vehicle connector.
